sources.ref_file_title: VZ12 - Characterizing Pseudoentropy and Simplifying Pseudorandom Generator Constructions

pages.class_justification: The HILL construction invokes the one-way function only as an oracle (many independent evaluations, universal hashing, Goldreich–Levin bits), and the security proof is a hybrid argument whose reduction runs any PRG distinguisher as an oracle to invert $f$: the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: Every [[hash-function|one-way function]] $f$ yields a [[pseudorandom-generator|pseudorandom generator]] $G$: the construction calls $f$ only as an oracle, and any efficient distinguisher for $G$ yields an efficient inverter for $f$ — [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]].
pages.sketch: From many independent evaluations of $f$, HILL extract bits with universal hashing and the Goldreich–Levin predicate [[GL89 - A Hard-Core Predicate for All One-Way Functions|GL89]]: $f(x)$ together with hashed bits of $x$ has pseudoentropy exceeding its entropy, and hashing across many independent copies converts the gap into pseudorandom output. A hybrid argument turns any distinguisher into an inverter for $f$.
pages.improvements_text:
- Seed length $\tilde{O}(n^4)$, with nonadaptive, parallelizable calls to $f$, via next-block pseudoentropy — [[HRV10 - Efficiency Improvements in Constructing Pseudorandom Generators from One-Way Functions|HRV10]]
- Seed length $\tilde{O}(n^3)$ and a simpler construction, via a characterization of pseudoentropy by hardness of sampling — [[VZ12 - Characterizing Pseudoentropy and Simplifying Pseudorandom Generator Constructions|VZ12]]
notes_to_keep: The hypothesis slug hash-function is the merged OWF/CRHF page, so the OWF node also owns collision resistance site-wide.
flags: GL89 removed from sources: it supplies the hard-core predicate (PRG from a one-way permutation) and does not prove OWF ⇒ PRG; the page's own migration notes call the joint citation a conflation. It stays cited from the sketch; the reference page exists.

The page's Notes contain the literal string 'Citations disagree across pages: [object Object]' — a migration artifact to delete.

sources.ref_file_title: BN00 - Authenticated Encryption Relations among Notions and Analysis of the Generic Composition Paradigm
sources.note: Canonical citation for encrypt-then-MAC (CPA-secure SKE + strongly unforgeable MAC ⇒ IND-CCA). Verified offline in vendor/cryptobib: AC:BelNam00, pp. 531-545, DOI 10.1007/3-540-44448-3_41; EPRINT:BelNam00 = 2000/025.

pages.class_justification: Every link is fully black-box: HILL's PRG uses the OWF only as an oracle, GGM's PRF uses the PRG only as an oracle, and $\Enc(k, m) = (r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ uses the PRF only as an oracle; each security reduction runs its adversary as an oracle, and fully-black-box reductions compose (RTV04).
pages.statement: Any [[hash-function|one-way function]] yields CPA-secure [[symmetric-key-encryption|SKE]]: the OWF gives a PRG — [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]] — the PRG gives a PRF — [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]] — and $\Enc(k, m) = (r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ for uniform $r$ is CPA-secure whenever $\Eval(k, \cdot)$ is a PRF — folklore. Encrypt-then-MAC with a strongly unforgeable [[message-authentication-code|MAC]] (a PRF suffices) upgrades the scheme to CCA security — [[BN00 - Authenticated Encryption Relations among Notions and Analysis of the Generic Composition Paradigm|BN00]].
notes_to_keep: The hypothesis slug hash-function is the merged OWF/CRHF page, so the OWF node also owns collision resistance site-wide.
flags: COMPOSITE: this edge compresses a chain whose links have their own pages (hash-function-to-prg-hill99, prg-to-prf-ggm86, prf-to-ske, mac-and-ske-to-cca-security); decide whether the compressed edge should remain alongside them.

Suspected-errors entry on impagliazzos-five-worlds line 63 lists this edge (as red-hf-to-ske) but the flagged error is the 'TDPs (equivalently, PKE or OT)' clause, not OWF ⇒ SKE; the claim here is unaffected.
Encrypt-then-MAC needs a strongly unforgeable MAC for generic IND-CCA (BN00); the deterministic PRF-based fixed-length MAC is strongly unforgeable.
BN00 is listed with role 'improvement' for lack of a better role: it sources the CCA extension in the statement, not an improvement of OWF ⇒ SKE.

sources.ref_file_title: BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity
sources.authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh, Michael Riabzev
Eli Ben-Sasson, Alessandro Chiesa, Nicholas Spooner
sources.note: Component, not chronological improvement: the ROM compiler from IOPs to succinct non-interactive arguments that BBHR18 use to remove interaction. Verified offline in vendor/cryptobib: pp. 31-60, DOI 10.1007/978-3-662-53644-5_2.

pages.class_justification: BBHR18 state no reduction class. Knowledge soundness of the non-interactive argument is proved in the random-oracle model, where the RTV axes do not apply cleanly; the standard-model interactive variant's CRHF-based reduction is not classified by the source either.
pages.model_justification: The non-interactive STARK compiles a FRI-based IOP with the BCS transform, whose knowledge soundness is proved in the random-oracle model ([[BCS16 - Interactive Oracle Proofs|BCS16]]); instantiating the oracle with a concrete hash is heuristic. Only the interactive variant reduces to collision resistance in the standard model, so `model: rom` is correct for the SNARK conclusion.
pages.statement: From a [[hash-function|collision-resistant hash function]] — used for Merkle commitments and modeled as a random oracle for non-interactivity — BBHR18 construct STARKs: transparent (no trusted setup) [[succinct-argument|succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge]] with quasilinear prover time and $O(\log^2 T)$ proof size for a $T$-step computation — [[BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity|BBHR18]].
pages.sketch: The execution trace is arithmetized into Reed–Solomon codewords, Merkle-committed with the hash function, and proximity-tested with FRI; the BCS transform compiles the resulting IOP into a non-interactive argument in the random-oracle model, preserving knowledge soundness.
pages.improvements_text: - Non-interactivity via the IOP-to-succinct-argument compiler in the random-oracle model — [[BCS16 - Interactive Oracle Proofs|BCS16]]
notes_to_keep: 'Security relies only on collision-resistant hash functions' in the source pages over-claims: non-interactive soundness needs the ROM, and the post-quantum claim additionally needs a QROM analysis.
The conclusion is the STARK variant, an alias/section of succinct-argument rather than its own slug.
flags: Duplicate BBHR18-sourced edges exist with different hypothesis sets (arithmetization-and-fri-fast-reed-solomon-iop-of-proximity-to-snark-bbhr18, arithmetization-to-snark-bbhr18, fri-fast-reed-solomon-iop-of-proximity-to-snark, hash-function-to-pcs-bbhr18); this page substitutes CRHF for AIR+FRI as the hypothesis — the family should be reconciled.

The wiki's 'prover time $O(T \log T)$' was generalized to 'quasilinear' in the statement: the exact bound could not be checked against the paper (eprint blocked). Proof size $O(\log^2 T)$ retained (FRI: $O(\log T)$ queries, each an $O(\log T)$ Merkle path).
BBHR18 is ePrint-only; the CRYPTO 2019 paper 'Scalable Zero Knowledge with No Trusted Setup' by the same authors is a distinct publication and should not be merged into this key.
verifier_changes: statement: 'prover time $O(T \log T)$' → 'quasilinear prover time' (unverifiable exact bound); tightened wording
tightened sketch, class_justification, model_justification and the BCS16 improvements bullet
BCS16 venue/pages/DOI recorded from cryptobib

sources.ref_file_title: BDH11 - XMSS A Practical Forward Secure Signature Scheme Based on Minimal Security Assumptions
sources.authors: Johannes Buchmann, Erik Dahmen, Andreas Hülsing
sources.note: Verified offline in vendor/cryptobib: PQCrypto 2011, pp. 117-129, DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-25405-5_8; ePrint 2011/484. Proves EU-CMA and forward security from a second-preimage-resistant hash function family and a pseudorandom function family.

sources.authors: Daniel J. Bernstein, Andreas Hülsing, Stefan Kölbl, Ruben Niederhagen, Joost Rijneveld, Peter Schwabe
sources.note: Verified offline in vendor/cryptobib: CCS:BHKNRS19, pp. 2129-2146; ePrint 2019/1086. Stateless variant (hypertree + FORS), standardized as SLH-DSA in FIPS 205.

pages.class_justification: XMSS calls the second-preimage-resistant hash family and the PRF only as oracles (Winternitz chains, L-trees, a Merkle tree), and the security reduction embeds a second-preimage or PRF challenge and runs any EU-CMA forger as an oracle — the standard hash-based-signature proof shape. BDH11 do not name an RTV class; the classification is from the proof shape.
pages.model_justification: BDH11's proof is in the standard model, with no random oracle. Parts of SPHINCS+'s concrete analysis use the (Q)ROM.
pages.statement: XMSS is a forward-secure many-time [[digital-signature#hash-based-signatures|hash-based signature scheme]] whose EU-CMA security reduces to second-preimage resistance of a [[hash-function|hash function]] family and pseudorandomness of a function family — [[BDH11 - XMSS A Practical Forward Secure Signature Scheme Based on Minimal Security Assumptions|BDH11]]. SPHINCS+ removes the state with a hypertree of XMSS-style subtrees and the few-time signature FORS at the leaves; NIST standardized it as SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) — [[BHK+19 - The SPHINCS+ Signature Framework|BHK+19]].
pages.sketch: A Winternitz one-time key signs each message; a Merkle tree over the one-time verification keys authenticates them under a single root public key, and bitmasked hashing lets second-preimage resistance replace collision resistance.
notes_to_keep: The frontmatter conclusion slug 'xmss' names a concrete scheme with no wiki page; the edge relates named artifacts, not model objects.
flags: Conclusion object mismatch: frontmatter says 'xmss' while the H1 and body link digital-signature#hash-based-signatures; consider a hash-based-signatures variant node or renaming the edge.

sources.note: Component: the statistically binding commitment from a PRG that instantiates GMW's commitment from any OWF.

sources.ref_file_title: HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function
sources.authors: Johan Håstad, Russell Impagliazzo, Leonid A. Levin, Michael Luby
sources.note: Component: PRG from any OWF, completing the OWF-only hypothesis.

pages.class_justification: The protocol uses a statistically binding commitment only as an oracle, and the commitment is built from any OWF via Naor's PRG-based scheme (Naor91 + HILL99), both fully black-box. Soundness is statistical; the zero-knowledge reduction converts any distinguisher of the simulation into a commitment-hiding distinguisher, hence an OWF inverter, running it as an oracle.
pages.statement: If [[hash-function|one-way functions]] exist, every language in $\classNP$ has a computational [[zero-knowledge-proof|zero-knowledge proof]] — [[GMW91 - Proofs that yield nothing but their validity or all languages in NP have zero-knowledge proof systems|GMW91]]. The protocol proves 3-colorability with a statistically binding commitment, which any OWF provides — [[Naor91 - Bit commitment using pseudorandomness|Naor91]], [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]].
pages.sketch: The prover commits to a uniformly permuted 3-coloring of the graph; the verifier picks a random edge and the prover opens its two endpoints, which must carry distinct colors. Sequential repetition drives the per-round soundness error $1 - 1/|E|$ down; a simulator that guesses the challenged edge and rewinds gives computational zero knowledge.
notes_to_keep: The conclusion is 'ZK proofs for all of NP', a language-class-qualified object the flat slug zero-knowledge-proof cannot express.
flags: GMW91's own theorem assumes a secure commitment/encryption; the OWF-only hypothesis follows by instantiating the commitment via Naor91 + HILL99, which postdate the conference version — standard citation practice, and the statement is written accordingly.
The frontmatter class fully-black-box is retained and justified from the construction shape; RTV04 does not formally treat ZK-for-NP as a primitive, so the classification is informal.
Possible overlap: content/Reductions/hash-function-to-czk.md (folklore, conclusion `czk`) may record the same result under a complexity-class conclusion.
verifier_changes: tightened statement, sketch and class_justification
added overlap flag for hash-function-to-czk

sources.ref_file_title: BDOZ11 - Semi-homomorphic Encryption and Multiparty Computation
sources.authors: Rikke Bendlin, Ivan Damgård, Claudio Orlandi, Sarah Zakarias
sources.note: Earlier: preprocessing from semi-homomorphic (additively homomorphic) encryption, UC-secure against a dishonest majority. Verified offline in vendor/cryptobib: EC:BDOZ11, pp. 169-188; EPRINT 2010/514.

pages.class_justification: SPDZ uses a concrete SHE scheme with distributed decryption and zero-knowledge proofs of plaintext knowledge, not an arbitrary HE scheme as an oracle, and neither source states an RTV class.
pages.statement: The offline phase of [[secure-multi-party-computation#mpc-with-preprocessing-spdz-etc|MPC with preprocessing]] can be instantiated from somewhat [[homomorphic-encryption|homomorphic encryption]]: SPDZ generates authenticated Beaver multiplication triples by depth-1 homomorphic evaluation under a shared SHE key with distributed decryption, giving an actively secure protocol against up to $n-1$ of $n$ corruptions whose online phase is unconditionally secure — [[DPSZ12 - Multiparty Computation from Somewhat Homomorphic Encryption|DPSZ12]]. The preprocessing can also be obtained from semi-homomorphic (additively homomorphic) encryption — [[BDOZ11 - Semi-homomorphic Encryption and Multiparty Computation|BDOZ11]].
pages.sketch: Parties encrypt random shares under a joint SHE public key, multiply ciphertexts homomorphically, and jointly decrypt to obtain additively shared, MAC-authenticated triples; the online phase consumes the triples to evaluate the arithmetic circuit with no further public-key operations.
flags: Hypothesis 'he' is coarser than the theorem: DPSZ12 need an SHE scheme supporting one multiplication plus distributed decryption and ZK proofs of plaintext knowledge; the wiki's HE node conflates PHE/SHE/FHE, so the edge overstates generality.
Conclusion 'mpc-with-preprocessing' is a section anchor of secure-multi-party-computation, not its own slug.

sources.ref_file_title: BL13 - Limits of Provable Security for Homomorphic Encryption
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified offline in vendor/cryptobib (C:BogLee13, LNCS 8042, pp. 111-128, DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-40041-4_7). The rerandomization result's exact hypothesis could not be read: eprint, ECCC and every index are egress-blocked; the researcher's account rests on search-result snippets.

pages.class_justification: BL13 state no reduction class; the rerandomizer runs the scheme's homomorphic evaluator, but the paper does not classify the transformation.
pages.statement: A public-key bit [[homomorphic-encryption|encryption scheme]] with a strong — distribution-preserving — homomorphic evaluator for a non-trivial boolean function is rerandomizable: a ciphertext can be mapped to one distributed as a fresh encryption of the same bit — [[BL13 - Limits of Provable Security for Homomorphic Encryption|BL13]]. BL13 use rerandomizability to place ciphertext distinguishing in $\classSZK$, bounding the provable security of such schemes; see [[no-he-to-szk-bl13|No reduction from HE to SZK]].
notes_to_keep: The migrated chain's second arrow (rerandomizable encryption → SZK ≠ BPP) is BL13's barrier content and lives on no-he-to-szk-bl13, not on this construction edge.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: the unqualified edge 'HE ⇒ RE' over-claims. BL13's rerandomization lemma needs a STRONG (distribution-preserving) homomorphic evaluator — a hypothesis compact/noise-based HE and FHE schemes need not satisfy — and no generic transformation from arbitrary HE is known. The statement adds the qualifier; the hypothesis node should be qualified or the edge re-scoped, else demoted to wrong_claim.

HIGH PRIORITY: the researcher's function-class condition 'essentially any boolean function (excluding constants, NOT, AND, OR)' was removed. It cannot be reconciled with strong evaluation (strong evaluation of AND with a fresh encryption of 1, or of NOT twice, rerandomizes), and its shape matches BL13's WEAK-evaluation 'sensitive collection' condition (the abstract lists 'the class of all AND and OR functions' as sensitive, implying a single AND is not). The statement now says 'non-trivial' and defers to the paper; a human with access to BL13 must fix the exact condition.

BL13 is chiefly a barrier paper (no provable security beyond AM ∩ coAM via adaptive reductions, or beyond SZK via constant-query reductions, for schemes with weak/compact evaluation of 'sensitive' collections); content/Barriers/no-he-to-szk-bl13.md already exists and should carry those theorems.
Rerandomizability from strong homomorphic evaluation is arguably an observation BL13 restate rather than originate; the page slug fixes BL13 as the source.
verifier_changes: statement: replaced the unverifiable exclusion list with 'non-trivial boolean function'; rerandomization described as 'distributed as a fresh encryption of the same bit' (what strong evaluation gives); barrier sentence now links no-he-to-szk-bl13
confidence high/medium → low; source note records what could and could not be verified
